mainTopic: The dangling limb and liquids that count at the moment of separation; רבי עקיבא's question about five offerings in one הֶעְלֵם, and רבי יהושע's קל וחומר from מעילה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a משנה about a limb still hanging from a living body. On ערב פסח, boil-sufferers in ירושלים had such a limb cut almost through and torn off on a thorn, so both the patient and the doctor stayed טהור for the קרבן פסח. The גמרא brings שמואל's rule that a wiped leek becomes מוכשר at the moment the water leaves it. It then asks why the dangling limb does not likewise make the patient טמא as it separates. The answer, borrowed from רב יוסף's explanation of a ברייתא about rain wrung from the clothes of a זב and a טמא מת, is that something torn away with full force has no moment of contact after separating. A new משנה follows, in which רבי עקיבא asks whether five offerings in one הֶעְלֵם bring one חטאת or five. In one version the case is slaughtering outside, and in רבי שמעון's version it is eating נותר. רבי יהושע answers with a קל וחומר from מעילה, and רבי עקיבא refutes it, because מעילה has strict rules that נותר lacks. The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's version, then asks whether רבי יהושע accepted the refutation. It brings a ברייתא where the first view makes him liable for each offering, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה requires only one חטאת.

steps.title: How the boil-sufferers in Jerusalem removed a dangling limb
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes a practice: on ערב פסח a doctor would cut a boil-sufferer's dangling limb until only a hair's width held it. He then stuck the limb on a thorn, and the patient pulled away.
steps.simpleTranslation: People with boils in ירושלים would do this: on ערב פסח each one went to the doctor. The doctor cut the limb until only a hair's width of it stayed attached. Then he stuck it on a thorn, and the patient pulled himself away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a real-life practice to show that a limb still hanging from a living person does not make anyone טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the limb is still attached, even by a hair, it does not make anyone טמא. The thorn trick lets the limb come off completely without the patient or the doctor touching it after it is detached.

keyTerms.meaning: people suffering from boils (a skin disease)
the day before פסח, when the קרבן פסח is brought
like a hair's width, a tiny bit
a thorn

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody touches the limb after it is fully cut off. The doctor only handles it while it is still attached, and the patient pulls away from it rather than taking hold of it.

phrases.english: people afflicted with boils would do this in Jerusalem:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹלֵךְ לוֹ עֶרֶב פֶּסַח אֵצֶל הָרוֹפֵא,
phrases.english: he would go on Passover eve to the doctor,
and he would cut it until he left it attached by a hair's width,
and he would stick it onto a thorn,
and the patient would pull away from it,

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A limb still hanging from a living person, even by a hair, does not make anyone טמא. It can then be separated without anyone touching it.

steps.title: Both bring the קרבן פסח, and a קל וחומר to an animal's limb
steps.stepSummary: Both the patient and the doctor stay טהור and bring their קרבן פסח. The משנה then says the same rule follows by קל וחומר for an animal's limb.
steps.simpleTranslation: That patient brings his קרבן פסח, and the doctor brings his קרבן פסח. And I see that this is a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה draws its conclusion: neither man became טמא. It then uses this case to prove, by קל וחומר, that a dangling limb on an animal is also טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A limb cut off a person has a strict טומאה, yet while it is dangling it is טהור. So a limb cut off an animal, whose טומאה is lighter, should surely be טהור while it is dangling.

keyTerms.meaning: his קרבן פסח (Pesach offering)
reasoning from a stricter case to a lighter one: if the strict case is so, surely the lighter one is
that person (here, the patient)

steps.whatToRemember: A limb still attached, even by a hair, is טהור. By קל וחומר from a person, the same is true of an animal's dangling limb.

phrases.english: and that one brings his Passover offering
and the doctor brings his Passover offering,
and I see that these matters follow by a kal vachomer.
phrases.notes: He reasons from a person's dangling limb to an animal's dangling limb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the practice described in step 1 and extends it to animals.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both stay טהור for the קרבן פסח, and a dangling animal limb is טהור by קל וחומר.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes a משנה about wiping a leek and squeezing hair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting a משנה from מכשירין. Water left inside a leek, hair or clothing is not הכשר, but the water that comes out is.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: if someone wipes a leek, or squeezes his hair or his clothing, the liquid still inside is not counted under 'כי יותן'. But the liquid that comes out is counted under 'כי יותן'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה from another מסכת. This is setting up the next move, where שמואל adds a comment on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquid only makes food able to become טמא when the owner wants it. By wiping or squeezing, the person shows he cares about the water that comes out, so that water counts. The water he leaves inside does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: a leek
squeezes out
'if water is put' (ויקרא 11:38): the rule that liquid can make food able to become טמא

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת מכשירין.

phrases.english: one who wipes the water off a leek,
or who squeezes his hair or his clothing,
the liquid still inside it is not under 'if it be put',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:38. 'כי יותן' is the rule for liquid that makes food able to become טמא.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיּוֹצְאִין מִמֶּנּוּ הֲרֵי הֵן בְּ״כִי יוּתַּן״.
phrases.english: but the liquid that comes out of it is under 'if it be put'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins its discussion by bringing an outside source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liquid wiped or squeezed out is הכשר. Liquid left inside is not.

steps.title: שמואל: the leek itself becomes susceptible
steps.stepSummary: שמואל adds that the leek itself also becomes מוכשר, able to become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: and the leek itself has become מוכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds something the משנה did not say: the leek itself, not just the water that came out, is now able to become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that once the water is wiped off, the leek is dry and nothing happened to it. שמואל says the leek did become מוכשר, and the גמרא will now ask why.

keyTerms.meaning: became מוכשר, able to become טמא
itself

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
and the leek itself has become susceptible,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new detail to the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wiped leek itself becomes able to become טמא.

steps.title: The reason: it becomes susceptible at the moment the water leaves
steps.stepSummary: Why is the leek מוכשר? Because at the very moment the water separates from it, that water is already a liquid the person wants, and it is still touching the leek.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? At the moment the water separates from it, the leek becomes מוכשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל holds this and answers: the leek becomes מוכשר right at the moment the water leaves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the person wipes, the water that comes out counts as הכשר. At the instant it is leaving, that water is still touching the leek, so it makes the leek מוכשר on its way out.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
at the moment of separating

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the leek becomes מוכשר at the very moment the water separates from it.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
At the moment of separation from it, it became susceptible.
phrases.notes: The water is already counted as wanted while it is still on the leek, so it makes the leek מוכשר as it leaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind שמואל's ruling in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the leek itself become מוכשר?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because at the moment the water separates, it already counts as הכשר and makes the leek מוכשר.

steps.title: The dangling limb should make the person impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא uses the ערב פסח case from our משנה to attack שמואל's idea that something counts at the very moment it separates.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in our משנה: on ערב פסח he goes to the doctor, and both stay pure. If you say the leek becomes מוכשר at the moment the water separates, then the same should apply to the dangling limb. At the moment it separates from the person, it should make him טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל from our משנה. If separation counts while the thing is still touching, then the limb should make the patient טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, the leek became מוכשר because the water was already counted as liquid while still touching it. Apply that logic to the limb: at the moment it comes off, it is already a separated limb, which carries טומאה, and it is still touching the person. Yet our משנה says the patient stays טהור, which seems to contradict שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: a dangling limb, hanging by a thread
at the moment they separate
became able to receive טומאה (מוכשר)
it should make him impure

phrases.english: But we learned: on Passover eve
he goes to [the doctor], etc.
phrases.notes: This is our own משנה from step 1, where both the patient and the doctor stay pure.

phrases.english: And if you say that at the moment of their separation it becomes susceptible,
phrases.notes: He means שמואל's leek: it becomes מוכשר the moment the water separates.

phrases.aramaic: הָא אִיכָּא נָמֵי הָהוּא אֵבֶר הַמְדוּלְדָּל,
phrases.english: then there is also that dangling limb,
at the moment of its separation from the person,
it should make the person impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning given in step 5 for שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that something counts as separated while it is still touching at the moment of separation.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same logic applied to the limb would make the patient טמא, against our משנה's ruling that he stays טהור.

steps.title: The limb is pulled off with full force
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב יוסף's principle: when something comes off with full force, there is no moment of separated contact.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף said: it is a case where they fly off with full force. Here too, the limb flies off with full force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by borrowing an idea from רב יוסף. The limb in our משנה comes off with one strong pull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The patient yanks himself away, so the limb snaps off all at once. There is no moment when it is a separated limb still touching him. Wiping water off a leek is gradual, so the drops do count while still touching, and שמואל's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: flying off, spraying off
with all their force
here too

phrases.english: As Rav Yosef says:
it is where they fly off with all their force,
here too,
it is where they fly off with all their force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: a forceful separation versus a gradual one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The limb should count as separated while still touching the patient, just like the water on the leek.
steps.terutzMaskana: A limb pulled off with full force has no moment of separated contact, so the patient stays טהור.

steps.title: Where did רב יוסף say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the original context of רב יוסף's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where was רב יוסף's statement said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רב יוסף first made his statement. This sets up the next step, which quotes the ברייתא he was explaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's idea was just borrowed for our case. Now the גמרא goes back to show the original case, so we can see what the idea first meant.

keyTerms.meaning: where was it said?

phrases.english: And where was the statement of Rav Yosef said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the principle used in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The original case on which רב יוסף said 'they fly off with full force'.

steps.title: The rain on the זב and the טמא מת
steps.stepSummary: The source is a ברייתא: rainwater squeezed and moving inside a garment stays טהור until it fully comes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: On this: a זב and a טמא מת were walking, and rain fell on them. Even though they squeeze each other's clothes, liquid moving from the upper part to the lower part stays pure. It is only counted as liquid once it has come out completely.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting the ברייתא that רב יוסף was explaining. Rainwater still moving inside a garment does not become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people wearing these garments are טמא, yet the water flowing within the cloth stays טהור. The reason is that it is not yet counted as liquid until it has fully left the garment.

keyTerms.meaning: a man made impure by a discharge
a person impure from a dead body
squeezing (wringing out)
liquids

phrases.english: On this: a zav and one impure from a corpse
who were walking
and rain fell on them,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁסּוֹחֲטִין זֶה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: even though they wring out one another,
phrases.notes: They are wringing the rain out of each other's clothes.

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁקִין הַיּוֹרְדִין מִצַּד הָעֶלְיוֹן לְצַד הַתַּחְתּוֹן –
phrases.english: the liquids going down from the upper side to the lower side
are pure,
since they only count once they have come out of all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהָא: זָב וּטְמֵא מֵת שֶׁהָיוּ מְהַלְּכִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 by quoting the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב יוסף was explaining the ברייתא about rain squeezed from the clothes of a זב and a טמא מת.

steps.title: Once out, the water makes food susceptible
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: once the water has fully come out, it is מכשיר, because it only counts after leaving the garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once it has come out completely, it makes things susceptible, because it is only counted after it has come out of the garment itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its rule. Water fully squeezed out of the garment does count, and it makes food able to become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Squeezing shows the people want this water out, so once it is out it counts as a wanted liquid and is מכשיר. The key point is when it starts to count: only after it has left the garment, not while it is coming out. That sounds like the opposite of שמואל's leek, which sets up רב יוסף's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: they make food able to become impure
they are counted (as liquid)
its body, here the garment itself

phrases.english: Once they have come out of all of it, they make things susceptible,
because they are not counted except
after they have come out of its body.
phrases.notes: 'Its body' means the garment the water was squeezed from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Squeezed water becomes מכשיר only once it has fully left the garment.

steps.title: רב יוסף: here the water flew off with force
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains the ברייתא as a case where the water sprays out forcefully.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: this is where the water flies out with full force.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains why, in the ברייתא, the water does not count while it is still coming out. This is the original place of the statement used in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, as with שמואל's leek, liquid counts the moment it separates, while still touching. The ברייתא says it only counts after it has left, so רב יוסף limits it to water that shoots out with force and has no moment of touching. This is exactly why the same idea worked for the limb in step 7.
steps.whatToRemember: Gradual separation, like water wiped off a leek, counts while still touching. Forceful separation, like a limb yanked off or water sprayed out, does not, so the patient on ערב פסח stays טהור.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is where they fly off with all their force.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: בְּנִיתָּזִין בְּכׇל כֹּחָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ruling of the ברייתא in steps 9 and 10, completing the answer to step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a case of forceful separation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to say liquid never counts at the moment of separation, against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of water that sprays out with force, so it fits with שמואל's rule for gradual separation.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks about slaughtering five offerings outside
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents רבי עקיבא's question: if someone slaughters five offerings outside the מקדש during one lapse of awareness, does he bring one חטאת or five? The sages answer that they have no tradition about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי עקיבא also asked them: If someone slaughters five offerings outside the מקדש during one lapse of awareness, what is the law? Is he liable for each one, or only once for all of them? They said to him: We have not heard.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. רבי עקיבא asks how many חטאות a person brings for five forbidden slaughterings done during one period of forgetting, and the sages admit they have no received answer. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether five separate offerings count as five separate sins, even though the person never remembered in between. The sages' answer, 'we have not heard,' leaves the door open for someone to work it out with reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה.' A new משנה is starting.
Slaughtering an offering outside the מקדש, which is forbidden.
One lapse of awareness. The person did all the acts without remembering in between that they were forbidden.
Liable for each and every one, meaning a separate חטאת for each act.
'We have not heard.' They have no tradition from their teachers on this case.

steps.confusionAlert: Normally, sins done during one lapse of awareness can be covered by one חטאת. The question is whether five different offerings break that up into five separate sins.

phrases.english: MISHNA
And furthermore, Rabbi Akiva asked them:
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'they asked' (round brackets). The corrected wording in square brackets says 'he asked them,' meaning רבי עקיבא was the one asking.

phrases.english: One who slaughters five offerings outside [the Temple]
during one lapse of awareness, what is the law?
Is he liable for each and every one,
or one for all of them?
They said to him: We have not heard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, separate from the earlier discussion of רב יוסף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An open question: are five outside slaughterings during one הֶעְלֵם one sin or five? There is no tradition on it.

steps.title: רבי יהושע derives the answer from מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says he has a tradition about מעילה: someone who eats from one offering taken from five pots during one lapse is liable separately for each pot. He argues by קל וחומר that five separate offerings should surely also be counted separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: I have heard that someone who eats from one offering, from five pots, during one lapse of awareness, is liable for each one because of מעילה. And I see that this can be learned by a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע fills the gap with something he did hear, a rule about מעילה. He uses it to answer רבי עקיבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מעילה case there is only one offering, yet the five pots make five separate liabilities. So with five completely separate offerings, there should surely be five separate liabilities. That is the קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: Pots or dishes. Here, the five pots the offering's meat was cooked in.
Misusing sacred property, which requires a קרבן אשם.
A 'how much more so' argument from a lighter case to a stronger case.
'I have heard,' meaning I have a tradition from my teachers.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a sage can answer a new question by reasoning from a known case when there is no direct tradition.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said: I have heard
regarding one who eats from one offering
from five pots during one lapse of awareness

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת
phrases.english: that he is liable for each and every one
due to misuse of sacred property,
and I consider that these matters are an a fortiori inference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's open question with a קל וחומר.
steps.raayaObject: That someone who slaughters five offerings outside during one הֶעְלֵם is liable separately for each one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע's tradition that eating one offering from five pots during one הֶעְלֵם brings separate liabilities for מעילה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון gives a different version of the question: eating נותר
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says רבי עקיבא did not ask about slaughtering outside. He asked about someone who eats נותר from five offerings during one lapse. The sages again say they have no tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: That is not what רבי עקיבא asked. He asked about someone who eats נותר from five offerings during one lapse of awareness. Is he liable once for all of them, or for each one? They said to him: We have not heard.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון reports the same story with a different case inside רבי עקיבא's question. This sets up רבי יהושע's answer, which comes again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question itself stays the same: do five separate offerings mean five separate sins during one lapse? Only the sin changes, from slaughtering outside to eating נותר.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of an offering left past its allowed time. Eating it is forbidden.
'That is not what he asked.' A different version of the question.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not arguing about the answer. He is only correcting which case רבי עקיבא asked about.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא כָּךְ שָׁאַל(ו) רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: Rabbi Akiva did not ask this,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the extra letter in round brackets, making it 'they asked.' The corrected wording reads 'he asked.'

phrases.english: rather, regarding one who eats notar from five offerings
during one lapse of awareness, what is the law?
Is he liable once for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת?
phrases.english: or is he liable for each and every one?
They said to him: We have not heard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֹא כָּךְ שָׁאַל רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the case in רבי עקיבא's question from step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the question was about eating נותר from five offerings during one הֶעְלֵם, and there was no tradition on it.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's same קל וחומר applied to נותר
steps.stepSummary: In רבי שמעון's version, רבי יהושע gives the same answer. He uses the מעילה rule about one offering in five pots to prove there are separate liabilities for eating נותר from five offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: I have heard that someone who eats from one offering in five pots during one lapse of awareness is liable for each one because of מעילה. And I see that this can be learned by a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats רבי יהושע's answer word for word. Now it answers the נותר version of the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning is the same. If one offering split into five pots already makes five liabilities for מעילה, then נותר eaten from five separate offerings should surely make five liabilities. Both versions of the story end with the same proof.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I see' or 'I consider.' He is giving his own reasoning, not a tradition he received.
'In five pots.' A slightly different wording of 'from five pots' with the same meaning.

steps.whatToRemember: In both versions of רבי עקיבא's question, slaughtering outside and eating נותר, רבי יהושע offers the same קל וחומר from מעילה: five separate offerings should mean five separate liabilities. The next steps show that רבי עקיבא refutes this proof.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said: I have heard
regarding one who eats from one offering
in five pots during one lapse of awareness

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת
phrases.english: that he is liable for each and every one
due to misuse of sacred property,
and I consider that these matters are an a fortiori inference.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שָׁמַעְתִּי בְּאוֹכֵל מִזֶּבַח אֶחָד בַּחֲמִשָּׁה תַּמְחוּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's version of the question with the same קל וחומר as step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That someone who eats נותר from five offerings during one הֶעְלֵם is liable separately for each one.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מעילה tradition about eating one offering from five pots during one הֶעְלֵם.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks whether this is a tradition or a logical proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא tells רבי יהושע that he will accept a received הלכה, but if this is only a logical proof, he has a refutation. רבי יהושע invites him to give it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: If it is a tradition, we will accept it. If it is a logical argument, there is a response. He said to him: Respond.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא signals that he is about to attack רבי יהושע's קל וחומר. This step sets up the actual refutation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of sources here. A הלכה received from one's teachers cannot be argued with. A דין, meaning a logical derivation like a קל וחומר, can be knocked down if it has a weak point. רבי עקיבא is not rejecting the conclusion yet. He is only saying the proof is open to challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A received tradition from one's teachers, accepted without argument
A logical derivation, such as a קַל וָחוֹמֶר, which can be challenged
Here: a refutation or rebuttal of an argument

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע already said he had a tradition, but that tradition was only about מעילה. The step from מעילה to נותר was his own קל וחומר. That logical step is the part רבי עקיבא challenges.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
If it is a tradition, we will accept it;
if it is a logical argument, there is a response.
He said to him: Respond.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הֲלָכָה נְקַבֵּל אִם לָדִין יֵשׁ תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יהושע's קל וחומר from מעילה in step 15 by announcing that it can be refuted.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Announces a coming rejection of the קל וחומר itself, not of a received tradition.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not stated yet. רבי עקיבא only says that a logical derivation is open to refutation.

steps.title: Misuse has special strict rules that leftover meat lacks
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא refutes the קל וחומר. מעילה is stricter than נותר in several ways: one who feeds another is treated like one who eats, one who gives benefit is treated like one who benefits, and small amounts combine over a long time. נותר has none of these rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: No. You spoke of misuse, where the Torah treated one who feeds another like one who eats, and one who gives benefit like one who benefits, and joined misuse done over a long time. Would you say the same about leftover meat, which has none of these rules?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives his actual refutation. He shows that מעילה is stricter than נותר, so you cannot learn נותר from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the source case is not stricter in some other way. מעילה has three strict rules that נותר lacks: the one who feeds is liable, the one who gives benefit is liable, and amounts eaten at different times combine. Since מעילה is stricter, its rule of separate liabilities may come from that strictness and may not carry over to נותר.

keyTerms.meaning: Misuse of consecrated property for personal use
One who feeds another person
One who gives another person benefit from consecrated property
Combining small amounts into one liable amount
Sacrificial meat left over past its permitted time

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר is refuted by showing that the source case has its own special strictness. Here מעילה has three strict rules that נותר lacks.
steps.whyThisMatters: This knocks out רבי יהושע's proof for נותר from five offerings. Steps 25–29 then ask whether רבי יהושע accepted this refutation, and bring a ברייתא to find out.

phrases.english: He said: No. If you said this about misuse,
where it made one who feeds another like one who eats,
and one who gives benefit like one who derives benefit,
and joined misuse done over a long period of time,

phrases.aramaic: תֹּאמַר בְּנוֹתָר, שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אַחַת מֵאֵלּוּ.
phrases.english: would you say the same about leftover meat, which has none of these?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Delivers the refutation announced in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the קל וחומר from מעילה to נותר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מעילה is stricter than נותר in three ways (feeding, giving benefit, combining over time). So its rule of separate liabilities cannot be carried over to נותר.

steps.title: What bothered רבי שמעון about the first version?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens and asks why רבי שמעון rejected the version where רבי עקיבא asked about slaughtering outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What was difficult for רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends here and the גמרא begins. It asks why רבי שמעון changed the question from slaughtering outside to eating נותר. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 12), the question was about slaughtering outside the מקדש. רבי שמעון insisted the question was about eating נותר (step 14). The גמרא wants to know what problem in the first version pushed him to say this.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
What was difficult for him? The גמרא asks what made a sage take his position

phrases.english: Gemara:
What was difficult for Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא, looking back at the two versions of רבי עקיבא's question in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי שמעון rejected the version of the question about slaughtering outside.

steps.title: You cannot prove slaughtering from eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון was bothered by the first version's proof. It learned a rule about slaughtering from a rule about eating, but an eater gets benefit and a slaughterer does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what was difficult for him: What proof can there be for one who slaughters from one who eats? What about one who eats? He is different, because he derives benefit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's problem. In the first version, רבי יהושע's proof from מעילה was about eating, but the question was about slaughtering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's proof involved someone eating from five pots. Eating gives the person benefit, and that could be why each act is counted separately. Slaughtering outside gives no physical benefit, so the proof does not fit. That is why רבי שמעון says the question must have been about eating נותר, where the proof matches.

keyTerms.meaning: One who slaughters (here: an offering outside the מקדש)
One who derives benefit
"What about X, which is different because...": the standard way to refute a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's version makes sense because a proof about eating can only teach about eating. Eating gives benefit, and slaughtering does not.

phrases.english: This is what was difficult for him:
What proof is there for one who slaughters from one who eats?
What about one who eats? He is different, because he derives benefit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the first version, a proof about eating was used for a question about slaughtering. That does not work, because eating gives benefit and slaughtering does not. So רבי שמעון said the question was about eating נותר.

steps.title: What רבי עקיבא really asked, according to רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Since the version about slaughtering outside had a weak proof, the גמרא says the question must have been about eating נותר from five offerings in one הֶעְלֵם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is how he asked them: if someone eats נותר from five offerings during one lapse of awareness, what is the law? Is he liable for each one, or only once for all of them? They said: We have not heard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from the last step. Since the slaughtering version does not work, it shows the question רבי עקיבא really asked according to רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 19 the גמרא said a slaughtering rule cannot be learned from an eating rule. So רבי שמעון makes the question about eating: eating נותר. Now the proof from eating in מעילה matches an eating question.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of an offering left past the time it may be eaten. Eating it is forbidden.
Animal offerings
One lapse of awareness. He did it all during one stretch of forgetting, without realizing in between.
We have not heard a ruling from our teachers

phrases.english: Rather, this is how he asked them:
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'they asked' (round brackets). The corrected wording in square brackets says 'he asked them', meaning רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: One who eats notar from five offerings
during one lapse of awareness, what is the law?
Is he liable for each and every one,
or only one for all of them?
They said to him: We have not heard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of Step 19 by showing the question that fits רבי שמעון's view
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question was about eating נותר from five offerings, so the proof from eating in מעילה fits.

steps.title: רבי יהושע spells out the קל וחומר from מעילה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע heard that one who eats from one offering in five pots brings a separate אשם for each pot. So five separate offerings should surely bring separate חטאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said: I heard that someone who eats from one offering out of five pots in one lapse of awareness is liable for each pot because of מעילה. I see a קל וחומר here. If one offering, which is not separate bodies, makes him liable for each pot just because the pots are separate, then five offerings, which are separate bodies, surely make him liable for each one!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers the question with a proof. He builds a קל וחומר from a known rule of מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מעילה, even one animal split into five pots counts as five separate eatings. Five different animals are separated even more strongly, by their own bodies. So it should be 'all the more so' that eating נותר from them counts as five separate sins.

keyTerms.meaning: Pots or dishes the meat was cooked or served in
Misusing holy property. It requires an אשם.
A 'how much more so' argument: if the lighter case has a rule, the stronger case surely does
Separate bodies, meaning separate animals
Is it not all the more so?

steps.whyThisMatters: This קל וחומר is exactly what רבי עקיבא will attack next by showing that מעילה is stricter than נותר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said: I have heard
about one who eats from one offering from five pots
during one lapse of awareness

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁחַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת מִשּׁוּם מְעִילָה,
phrases.english: that he is liable for each and every one because of misuse of holy property,
and I see that these matters follow by a how-much-more-so argument:
Just as from one offering,
where the bodies are not separate,
he is liable for each and every one
because the pots are separate,
then five offerings, which are separate bodies,
is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20 with a proof
steps.raayaObject: That eating נותר from five offerings in one הֶעְלֵם requires five חטאות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rule that eating from one offering in five pots brings five אשמות for מעילה, turned into a קל וחומר

steps.title: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's words in the משנה again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting the משנה: רבי שמעון says the question was about eating נותר from five offerings, and the sages had not heard an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: That is not what he asked. Rather, he asked about one who eats נותר from five offerings in one lapse of awareness: is he liable once for all of them, or for each one? They said: We have not heard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new discussion. It quotes the משנה's words of רבי שמעון again so it can look closely at what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question as Step 20, but now it is quoted straight from the משנה. Notice the two options are listed in the opposite order here: 'one for all' comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not ask it this way. רבי שמעון is correcting the other version.
Liable for only one offering for everything

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. The גמרא is quoting the משנה again to start discussing it, so do not count this as a third version.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא כָּךְ שָׁאַל(ו),
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said: That is not what he asked,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the letter in round brackets, which makes it 'they asked'. Without it, it means רבי עקיבא asked.

phrases.english: rather, about one who eats notar
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words 'from one offering' in round brackets, but the corrected wording leaves them out, since the case is five offerings.

phrases.english: from five offerings during one lapse of awareness, what is the law?
Is he liable once for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת?
phrases.english: or is he liable for each and every one?
They said to him: We have not heard.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: לֹא כָּךְ שָׁאַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section by quoting the משנה again
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the question was about eating נותר from five offerings in one הֶעְלֵם, and no tradition was known.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's answer from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה, רבי יהושע says he heard the מעילה rule about one offering in five pots, and he sees a קל וחומר from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: I heard that someone who eats from one offering in five pots is liable for each one because of מעילה, and I see that this matter follows by a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the משנה. This is רבי יהושע's short answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says 'קל וחומר' without explaining it. The full reasoning is the one spelled out in Step 21. Here רבי יהושע frames it as his own reasoning, which sets up רבי עקיבא's reply.

keyTerms.meaning: I see, meaning it is my own reasoning and not a received tradition
I have heard from my teachers

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: I have heard
about one who eats from one offering in five pots,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת
phrases.english: that he is liable for each and every one
because of misuse of holy property,
and I see that these matters follow by a how-much-more-so argument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the משנה with the answer to the question in Step 22
steps.raayaObject: Separate liability for each offering of נותר
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מעילה rule about one offering in five pots

steps.title: רבי עקיבא starts his reply
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא begins: if this is a received הלכה, we will accept it. The rest of his words are cut short with 'etc.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: If it is a received הלכה, we will accept it, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes only the start of רבי עקיבא's reply and cuts it short, setting up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא draws a line: a tradition from teachers he will accept, but a קל וחומר can be challenged. The full refutation, that מעילה is stricter than נותר, appears in the משנה (Step 17).

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a ruling received from one's teachers, not worked out by logic
We will accept it
Short for 'etc.': the rest of the quote is in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's version moves the question to eating נותר so that the proof from eating in מעילה fits. Even so, רבי עקיבא will only accept a received tradition, not this קל וחומר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
If it is a received law, we will accept it, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the challenge to רבי יהושע's קל וחומר from Step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the logical proof. A received tradition would be accepted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Hinted here and spelled out in the משנה: מעילה has stricter rules than נותר, so the קל וחומר fails.

steps.title: Did רבי יהושע accept רבי עקיבא's answer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יהושע accepted the refutation that רבי עקיבא gave him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יהושע accept this refutation from רבי עקיבא, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the debate in the משנה: did רבי יהושע agree with רבי עקיבא's answer? This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע built a קל וחומר from the מעילה rule, and רבי עקיבא pushed back. The משנה never says how רבי יהושע responded, so the גמרא wants to know whether he dropped his position.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, an answer that knocks down an argument
He accepted it

phrases.english: Did Rabbi Yehoshua accept
this refutation from Rabbi Akiva
phrases.notes: This is רבי עקיבא's pushback from step 17, quoted again in step 24, against רבי יהושע's קל וחומר.

phrases.english: or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַיבְּלַהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְהָא תְּשׁוּבָה מֵרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי עקיבא's refutation of רבי יהושע's קל וחומר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהושע gave up his position after רבי עקיבא's refutation.

steps.title: A ברייתא: one offering eaten from five pots
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that eating נותר from one offering in five pots during one הֶעְלֵם needs only one חטאת. If there were five separate הֶעְלֵמוֹת, he brings a separate offering for each.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: If someone ate five pieces of נותר from one offering, in one lapse of awareness, from five pots, he brings only one חטאת. If he is unsure whether he sinned, he brings only one אשם תלוי. If he ate from five pots in five lapses of awareness, he brings a חטאת for each one. If he is unsure, he brings an אשם תלוי for each one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. This first part covers eating from just one offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חטאת, having five pots does not split the sin into five. Only one offering and one הֶעְלֵם count, so he brings one חטאת. What does split it is having separate הֶעְלֵמוֹת, meaning he became aware of his sin between each eating.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of an offering left past the time it may be eaten
One lapse of awareness: he did not find out he sinned in between
Pots or dishes
A provisional guilt offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
A case where he does not know for sure that he sinned

steps.confusionAlert: Five pots do not mean five חטאות here. Only separate הֶעְלֵמוֹת can split the חטאת, and according to the ברייתא's first view, separate offerings can too. Pots matter for מעילה, which comes at the end.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
If he ate five pieces of notar
from one offering
in one lapse of awareness
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both just mean 'one.'

phrases.english: in five pots,
he brings only one sin offering,
and for their 'not known' case,
phrases.notes: He means: when he isn't sure whether he actually ate them sinfully.

phrases.english: he brings only a provisional guilt offering.
From five pots
in five lapses of awareness,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets comes from the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא חַטָּאת עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת,
phrases.english: he brings a sin offering for each and every one,
and for their 'not known' case,

phrases.aramaic: מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת.
phrases.english: he brings a provisional guilt offering for each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to answer the question of step 25.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהושע kept his view that separate offerings mean separate חטאות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about eating נותר from pots and offerings.

steps.title: Five different offerings in one lapse: liable for each
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's first view rules that eating from five separate offerings in one הֶעְלֵם makes him liable for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate from five offerings in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the key case: five different offerings eaten in one הֶעְלֵם. Its first view says each offering counts separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly רבי יהושע's position from the משנה: separate offerings are separate things, so each needs its own חטאת. Because a ברייתא states this as a ruling, it suggests the view was still held after רבי עקיבא's refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings (more than one)
Liable, here meaning a separate חטאת for each

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the case the debate between רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא was about, so it is the heart of the proof.

phrases.english: From five offerings
in one lapse of awareness, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with the case of separate offerings.
steps.raayaObject: The view that five offerings in one הֶעְלֵם require five חטאות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first view in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה: only one sin offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says that even five offerings in one הֶעְלֵם need only one חטאת and one אשם תלוי. Then a general rule ties חטאות and אשמות together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: Even if he ate five pieces from five offerings in one lapse of awareness, he brings only one חטאת. If he is unsure, he brings only one אשם תלוי. The general principle: whenever the sins count separately for חטאות, they count separately for אשמות.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the ברייתא disagrees with the case just given. It holds that separate offerings do not split the sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, it is all one prohibition, נותר, done in one הֶעְלֵם, so it is one sin no matter how many offerings were eaten. This is the opposite of רבי יהושע's conclusion. Note that רבי עקיבא only refuted his proof and did not himself rule this way. The closing rule says the אשם תלוי always follows the same counting as the חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A case where he is unsure about them
The general principle of the matter
Split, counted as separate

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
Even if he ate five pieces
from five offerings
in one lapse of awareness,
he brings only one sin offering,
and for the uncertain case of them,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מֵבִיא אֶלָּא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי אֶחָד.
phrases.english: he brings only one provisional guilt offering.
The principle of the matter:
whatever is split for sin offerings
is split for guilt offerings.
phrases.notes: He means the provisional guilt offerings, the אשם תלוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר אֲפִילּוּ אָכַל חָמֵשׁ חֲתִיכוֹת מֵחֲמִשָּׁה זְבָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling on five offerings in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five offerings in one הֶעְלֵם need only one חטאת and one אשם תלוי. The count of the אשם תלוי always follows the count of the חטאת.

steps.title: Five pots before the blood is sprinkled: liable for מעילה on each
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that eating from five pots of one offering before זריקת דמים makes him liable for מעילה on each piece, even in one הֶעְלֵם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he ate five pieces in five pots from one offering before the blood was sprinkled, even in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each and every one because of מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes with the מעילה rule, the same rule רבי יהושע used for his קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מעילה, the pots do split the sin, even in one הֶעְלֵם. For חטאת on נותר, they did not split it. This is the rule רבי יהושע said he had heard, and it is the base for his קל וחומר that five offerings should surely split the חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling the offering's blood on the מזבח, after which the meat may be eaten
Wrongly using holy property, which requires an אשם

steps.whatToRemember: In this ברייתא, pots split the count for מעילה but not for חטאת on נותר. For separate offerings, the first view says they split the חטאת, but רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says they do not.

phrases.english: If he ate five pieces
in five pots
from one offering
before the sprinkling of the blood,
even in one lapse of awareness,
he is liable for each and every one
because of misuse of holy property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָכַל חָמֵשׁ חֲתִיכוֹת בַּחֲמִשָּׁה תַּמְחוּיִין מִזֶּבַח אֶחָד לִפְנֵי זְרִיקַת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the מעילה rule that רבי יהושע relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating from five pots of one offering before זריקת דמים, even in one הֶעְלֵם, makes him liable for מעילה on each pot.
